title: Isolating DNA from Wolbachia and Drosophila with the Puregene Tissue Kit
author: Alphaxand Njogu
materials: Centrifuge tubes, 1.5 mL, safe-lock, PCR clean

(Optional) Dilute 20 µg/µL Glycogen, molecular biology grade Invitrogen Catalog #10814-010 to 0.5 µg/µL . Add 1 µL to each sample. Glycogen acts as a carrier molecule, improving DNA precipitation yield, particularly in low-biomass samples.

steps.title: Homogenize samples
steps.instruction: Transfer each 1.5 mL safe‑lock PCR tube containing the sample to a bead‑mill homogenizer and homogenize at 1500 rpm, room temperature, for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare lysis mixture
steps.instruction: In a clean 1.5 mL tube, combine per sample 300 µL cell lysis solution with 1.5 µL Proteinase K; prepare a slight excess to allow for pipetting error.

steps.title: Add lysis mixture
steps.instruction: Add 301.5 µL of the prepared lysis mixture to each sample tube.

steps.title: Cool samples on ice
steps.instruction: Place the tubes on an ice block and incubate for 1 minute to quickly cool the samples.

steps.title: Add protein precipitant and vortex
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL protein precipitation solution to each tube, then vortex immediately for 20 seconds; mixing must occur without delay.

steps.title: Pellet protein by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge tubes at 16 000 rpm, room temperature, for 3 minutes to pellet protein. If the pellet is not tight, incubate on ice for 5 minutes and repeat the centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: If pellet not tight, incubate on ice 5 min and repeat centrifugation

steps.title: Invert to mix tubes
steps.instruction: Invert each tube 25 times. For large batches, arrange tubes in a rack, place a second rack on top, and invert the whole stack simultaneously.

steps.title: Add isopropanol and transfer supernatant
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL molecular‑biology‑grade isopropanol (Fisher Scientific catalog #BP‑2618‑1) to a clean 1.5 mL tube and carefully transfer the supernatant from the previous step into the isopropanol by pipetting.

steps.title: Add ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL of 70 % (v/v) ethanol to each tube.

steps.title: Add DNA hydration solution
steps.instruction: Add 15–100 µL DNA hydration solution to each tube (use the lower volume for low‑biomass samples).

steps.title: Incubate for DNA elution
steps.instruction: Incubate tubes at 55 °C for 3 hours to 16 hours in a dry‑bath incubator; optionally place on a Thermomixer set to 300 rpm.

steps.title: Mix after incubation
steps.instruction: Invert each tube 50 times.

steps.title: Pellet DNA by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 16 000 rcf, room temperature, for 1 minute to pellet DNA.

steps.title: Discard supernatant and dry pellet
steps.instruction: Carefully pour the supernatant into a waste container, then drain the tube by a single rapid inversion onto a paper towel, ensuring the DNA pellet remains undisturbed.

substeps.instruction: Drain tube by a single rapid inversion onto paper towel, keeping pellet

steps.title: Resuspend pellet by inversion
steps.instruction: Invert the tubes 50 times.

steps.title: Second DNA centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge again at 16 000 rcf, room temperature, for 1 minute.

steps.title: Repeat wash (optional second)
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 14–16 once more to wash the pellet a second time.

steps.title: Vacuum‑dry DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Transfer tubes to a vacuum centrifuge and dry pellets for 10 minutes; if using a Vacufuge plus, select the D‑AL setting. Stop before the pellet becomes completely dry to avoid overdrying.

substeps.instruction: Dry for 10 min using D‑AL setting if Vacufuge plus
Stop before pellet becomes completely dry

steps.title: Vortex to break pellet
steps.instruction: Vortex each tube for 5 seconds to break up the DNA pellet.

steps.title: Dissolve DNA
steps.instruction: Choose either (a) incubate at 65 °C for 1 hour, or (b) incubate at room temperature overnight, to fully dissolve the DNA.

substeps.instruction: Incubate at 65 °C for 1 hour OR incubate at RT overnight

steps.title: Store DNA
steps.instruction: Use the DNA immediately or store at –80 °C for long‑term, –20 °C for a few weeks, or 4 °C for a few days.
